text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.1% today to $134.26, continuing a slide from its $137.20 peak two days ago. The immediate pressure comes from a sharp drop in U.S. crude oil prices—down to $91.48 per barrel from recent highs—even as global oil remains elevated at $96.02. That gap between U.S. and world prices suggests a supply glut building domestically, which weighs on the economics of U.S. oil producers like ConocoPhillips.

The broader headwind is political: Trump's reported deal to restore Venezuelan oil supplies to U.S. markets would increase crude available to refineries and dampen prices further, while simultaneous sanctions escalation against Iran (the EU formally joining the campaign) muddles longer-term supply dynamics. For an oil producer, near-term price pressure from potential Venezuelan supply overwhelms any benefit from tighter Iranian supplies down the line.
